 MISSOULA, Mont. — About 11,000 HAIARA power banks sold on Amazon are being recalled because their lithium-ion batteries can explode or catch fire, posing fire and burn hazards, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission.
 The recall involves HAIARA W5 PRO power banks sold by Mitrytech on Amazon from May 2025 through September 2026 for between $18 and $22.
 The black power banks have "20W" printed on the front and "Model: W5 PRO" on the side. The recall applies to units without a date code printed on the side.
 Mitrytech has received 600 reports of fires and other overheating incidents, including three reports of burn injuries and nine reports of property damage.
 Consumers should stop using the recalled power banks immediately and contact Mitrytech for a full refund.
 To receive a refund, consumers must submit a photo of the power bank marked "recalled" and confirm they have disposed of it in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
 Consumers can contact Mitrytech at HAIARArecall@outlook.com or visit the company's recall website for instructions.
